text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London finished lower, erasing earlier gains on light trade selling. US forecaster Weather Services Corporation said cold air building over Argentina on July 3 was expected to pass off to the south of Brazil's coffee belt as the warm, high pressure dominating the area continued its hold over the region. July lost $25 to close at $1,785 per tonne, while September gave up $55 to close also at $1,785 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York closed mostly lower in quiet dealings ahead of the long weekend in the US. Benchmark September futures lost 4.00 cents/lb to close at 168.35 cents/lb, while December closed 1 cent easier at 151.50 cents/lb. Predictions of a cold front had sparked a round of nervous buying earlier in the week, but the market quickly retreated once forecasters said the temperatures will remain above freezing levels in the coffee belt. Traders also noted the potential for a large build-up in the exchanges' certified inventories.

UNITED STATES - Certified coffee stocks rose by 725 60-kg bags as of July 2, to 50,550 bags, the CSCE said. An additional 37,295 bags were pending exchange approval. While there is no guarantee that the coffee will meet CSCE grading specifications, traders said they expected at least some of the coffee to be certified.

MEXICO - Mexico exported 4.125 million bags of coffee in October/June 1996/97 worth $798.4 million compared to 4.1 million bags exported the same period last year worth $595.5 million, the Mexican Coffee Council said. Production in 1996/97 (October/September) reached 5.1 million bags, down from 5.3 million bags produced the previous year.

FRANCE ** - France imported 652,612 bags of coffee in April 1997, 6.5 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 2.528 million bags, nearly 11 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 7 per cent to 6.696 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/April 1997 were Kenya (197,400 vs 244,600 bags), Uganda (217,400 vs 184,000 bags), Brazil (356,500 vs 214,600 bags), Colombia (183,300 vs 212,800 bags) and Vietnam (246,900 vs 146,700 bags).

The country exported 415,800 bags of coffee in January/April 1997, 7 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 10 per cent to 1.186 million bags.
